profile: A history reader interested in the Industrial Revolution, the Roman Empire and the history of science.
shelf: 1. The Steam Engine and the Age of Machines — Explains how the steam engine, refined over decades, freed factories from rivers and became the mechanical heart of the industrial revolution.
2. Cotton Mills of Lancashire — An essay on how the cotton mills of Lancashire depended on child labour and reshaped whole towns around the rhythm of the machine.

3. Children of the Factory Floor — A news-style report on child labour in the industrial revolution's cotton mills, and the campaign that finally brought railways of inspectors and reformers to the factory gates.

4. Iron Rails, Iron Will: Building Britain's Railways — A blog post celebrating how railways, powered by the steam engine, replaced the horse and stitched the country together faster than anyone expected.
5. The Roman Legions on the March — An essay on how the discipline of the Roman legions, more than any single general, held the Roman Empire together for centuries.
6. Roads That Built an Empire — An explainer on how the Roman Empire's road network, engineered to outlast the men who built it, bound distant provinces of the Roman Empire together.
7. The Fall of Rome, Revisited — An essay reconsidering why the Roman Empire's legions, once unbeatable, could no longer hold the frontier by the empire's final morning.
8. Hadrian's Wall: The Empire's Northern Edge — A blog post on Hadrian's Wall as the visible edge of the Roman Empire, patrolled by legions who traded the horse for a life on foot along the frontier.

9. The Royal Society and the Birth of Modern Science — An explainer on how the Royal Society turned scattered curiosity into a shared method, corresponding by letter about experiments including Darwin's later work on natural selection.
10. Newton's Quiet Revolution — An essay on how Isaac Newton, working largely alone, used the Royal Society and the printing press to turn private calculation into shared, lasting science.

11. Darwin's Voyage and the Idea of Natural Selection — A news-style account of how Charles Darwin's voyage supplied the evidence behind natural selection, which he later brought before the Royal Society and set in print by the printing press.

12. The Printing Press and the Spread of Ideas — An essay on how the printing press turned the rare, hand-copied book into an ordinary object, letting the Royal Society and ideas like natural selection reach a wide public.

13. Threads of Change: Cotton, Steam and the Factory Age — A blog post tying together the steam engine, the railways and the cotton mills of the industrial revolution, and the child labour that powered all three.
